text:
Devon: heads up — our metrics show a sharp spike in SNAT mappings in us-east-1 at 09:12 UTC, NAT gateway capacity nearing 100%.
Kumar: saw that. latency for model pulls jumped and bookkeeping errors in sidecars started surfacing.
Lisa: got logs? any pattern on which pools/pods? :thinking_face:
Devon: looks tied to batch model pulls from the new rollout — many pods open short-lived outbound TCP connections to S3/model-registry concurrently.
Devon: netstat dump from one node:
```
$ ss -s
TCP: total 32768 (estab 500, closed 30268, orphaned 0, timewait 29500)
sockets: 4096
``` 
Sam: time_wait is huge. Are we exhausting ephemeral ports / doing heavy 4-tuple churn? sounds like many short connections.
Kumar: AWS NATGW has ~64k ports per attached IP; when pod fanout multiplies by ENIs it still adds up fast. Also saw EIP rotation on some retries which recomposed SNAT tables.
ops-oncall: infra-bot alerted: "natgw-port-usage" threshold crossed for nat-eni-3 in az-a.
infra-bot: alert details -> peak ephemeral allocation 61,200, connection reset rate +18%.
Lisa: quick mitigation: can we enable connection reuse via an ingress sidecar that does HTTP/2 multiplexing to S3/registry? or put a local egress proxy per node?
Sam: we have haproxy sidecar prototype that keeps persistent upstreams and multiplexes requests. config snippet we used for keepalive:
```
defaults
  timeout client  30s
  timeout server  30s
frontend fe
  bind :8080
  mode http
backend s3_up
  mode http
  option http-server-close
  option http-keep-alive
  server s3 s3.amazonaws.com:443 check ssl verify none
```
Kumar: good. That will reduce new TCP handshakes. Also short-term we can increase node-level ephemeral port range and lower TIME_WAIT. e.g.:
```
sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="15000 65000"
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=15
```
Devon: agree but kernel tweaks are temporary and not ideal for long-term. We should avoid relying on tweaked host kernels for production infra.
Lisa: ops suggestion: route heavy model-fetch traffic through dedicated egress fleet (a pool of proxy VMs with larger EIP counts) and add rate limiting per pod.
Kumar: allocation plan: spin up 6 proxy instances with EIP-per-instance (x3 ENIs each) to reduce per-node SNAT pressure. Also configure HTTP/2 on proxies to multiplex.
Sam: can we do an emergency rollout? steps: 1) flag model-puller workload to use NODE_EGRESS_PROXY service via env var. 2) deploy 3 proxies in us-east-1a, 3 in 1b. 3) enable haproxy with keepalive + http2. 4) monitor natgw metrics.
ops-oncall: doing step 1 now — adding env var to canary namespace.
Devon: adding circuit-breaker on client side: exponential backoff + jitter and local request queueing to avoid synchronized retries.
Lisa: we'll also add a temporary k8s egress policy to redirect outbound traffic on port 443 to the local sidecar for canary; config in progress.
Kumar: added prometheus panel for ephemeral ports per nat-eni and connection resets by AZ. dashboard: link: https://grafana.internal/board/egress-ports
Sam: quick test results from canary (first 10m): per-node ephemeral usage down ~72%, natgw peak now 38k on problematic ENI.
Devon: nice. still seeing some TLS session churn — probably because model registry does not reuse session IDs across different clients. consider TLS session caching on proxy.
Lisa: haproxy supports ssl reuse via "ssl-server-verify none" and session-ticket caching. we'll enable.
ops-oncall: alert noise reduced. infra-bot reports natgw threshold below critical.
Kumar: next: prepare a runbook for long-term: 1) per-node egress proxy agent (sidecar) rollout for high-fanout jobs 2) dedicated egress pool with reserved EIPs 3) change orchestration to stagger model pulls (jitter start windows) 4) include port usage limits in cost/SLAs.
Devon: add a postmortem doc and owners. we should also quantify cost of dedicated egress vs increasing NATGW capacity.
Lisa: I'll draft the postmortem and include traffic histograms, kernel tweak implications, and the proxy config we used.
Sam: note — we saw one kube-proxy version where conntrack entries leaked after restarts. please file an infra bug if anyone can reproduce.
Kumar: filing bug #INF-4312 with logs and steps.
Devon: thanks team. leaving this thread open until we have the postmortem and runbook. :thumbsup:
Lisa: will post postmortem link when ready.
ops-oncall: closing alerts; will reopen if thresholds cross again.
